Its manifest records tests=none; the reviewed manifest's baseline_suite and after_suite gate fields are null (the reviewed run's own gate logs), so no base-arm/head-arm added-failure count exists to take. added_failure_count set to 0 and added_failure_ids to [] on that basis.

findings.text: The FAME q-scalar table records Q95 max +32.65, but the node's own fetch_channels read for E101154 returned max 32.3899 (the run transcript's tool result prints 'CH Q95 unit=... min 7.28663 max 32.3899 first 28.3207 last 7.28663', and the JSON block repeats max 32.389878031101716), and the node's own summary text in the same run states 'Q95 ... max 32.39'. The table value +32.65 is asserted beyond the logged read and disagrees with the node's own summary.

The FAME table header labels the two per-channel value columns 'first t' and 'last t', but the cells hold the first and last sample VALUES (QAXIS +0.9989 / +0.9982, a signed q, not a time, per-channel rows), so a reader can take the q value for a timestamp; the reader's own tool result labels the same two numbers simply 'first' and 'last'. Relabel the columns 'first'/'last' (values) or carry the sample times, so the header matches the cells.

The leads table states the Web API 'serves discharge and plant time series only ... not an equilibrium store', while the plan asked the node to learn 'whether it serves EQDB or FAME records'. The manual excerpt the node retrieved (pdftotext over /home/d240044/Code/jt60sa-agent/mindsdb/pdf/WEB API/WebAPI_UserGuide(rmssnd23)_EN_20240304.pdf, grepped for eqdb|fame|equilibrium) names the host and port and describes the API as an interface 'for downloading data', but names neither EQDB nor FAME; so 'not an equilibrium store' is the node's inference from the manual's download scope rather than the manual's statement, and should be qualified as such.

justifications.durability: The fragment is a static HTML whose key result - the reached and unreached leads - is stated in its own text, and the run's negative_control.log is present and openable, so the IRET 300 reproduction can be re-checked without the live host. Deduction: unlike the sibling nodes, this node kept no named probe logs on disk for the FAME read, the per-shot EQDB index table, the LOCALDB listing or the Web API manual read; those live only inside the FAME transcript under the run's harness/projects/ directory (a 2.7 MB jsonl), so re-verifying the fragment's numbers means reading the session transcript rather than a node-named log. The Q95 max error (see findings) shows the cost of that: the number that disagrees with the read is the one the durable artifact carries.
justifications.evidence: Every material claim traces to a call and its result in the run's session transcript: the FAME read returns 'SERVED 8 REFUSED 0' with each channel's first/last/min/max (QAXIS 0.87879..1.05636, QSURF 8.60424..97.6188, QEFF 6.25539..50.3525, TTCU 286006..998016, BTV 5.98505..6.02301, QSURF/QEFFFBI all 0); the per-shot GetTimeList table matches the fragment row for row (E100999 63 / 1 1 1 1, E101029 94 / 2 2 2 2, E101162 126 / 9 9 9 9, E101163 48 / 4 4 4 4, E101154 105, E100599/E100658/E101173 all 0, eqdb 5 always 0); the LOCALDB listing shows only EQDSK/10/1010/101011/{004000,004500} and the 101154 path returns False; the Web API manual names host rmssnd23.naka.qst.go.jp;157.111.196.190 port 50000. The reader is shown to see data (SERVED 8, and nonzero index counts beside the zero ones), so the empty EQDB field return is shown to be an absence, not a dead reader. Deductions: the fragment's Q95 max +32.65 contradicts the read's 32.3899 and the node's own summary's 32.39; the FAME table's 'first t'/'last t' columns hold values, not times.
justifications.fit: Every element id begins with the node id jtmm-equilibrium-source-leads (20 ids, zero outside the prefix, no duplicates), so sibling fragments composed into one record cannot collide on an anchor. The fragment parses as HTML. Names and prose describe the JT-60SA stores and the read mechanism, with no version, plan, sprint or ticket identifier and no author attribution.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The fragment answers the section 6 node question honestly: it states what each lead carries (FAME signed q scalars but no grid; EQDB psi on a 129x129 grid with QQV and profiles; EQRV/EQEFIT MSE-constrained; LOCALDB and FBEQU a single OP1 shot, 101011; LCDB/MBDB profile stores; the Web API a data service), which OP1 shots each store holds, and how intr26-2 reaches each one, with reads attempted. It reads the FAME q scalars for E101154 through fetch_channels and states their sign beside TTCU (Ip, +) and BTV (F=RxBT, +); it lists EQDB slice indices by shot for the whole identified OP1 list, not only E101154; it reads the Web API manual for the serving host. Deduction: the Web API conclusion ('not an equilibrium store') reads as a statement of the manual where the manual names neither EQDB nor FAME.
justifications.reuse: The node builds on the existing readers and its predecessor fragments rather than re-deriving them: it reads the FAME scalars through the existing RemoteEddbExtractor.fetch_channels, the EQDB indices through the shipped eqread_pac/FleddTool over the prebuilt libFLEDDPIC.so, and the shot list from jtmm-op1-shot-survey.json rather than re-sweeping; it corroborates the route-search and eqdb-entry-probe findings (dbsvr17p unreachable, LOCALDB/FBEQU shot 101011) rather than contradicting them. Deduction: it restates the dbsvr17p unreachability already established by the sibling fragments where a reference would have sufficed.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat b839dae7..b6a5eceb and the commit's own --stat list exactly one changed file, docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-machine-map/jtmm-equilibrium-source-leads.html (202 insertions), which is the manifest's declared changed_path and within the node's declared write scope; no product source and no test is touched, matching the plan's 'writes one fragment and no source'. The node stayed read-only on nakasvr26, one ssh at a time, no home but /home/d240034, no keys/credentials/history. git merge-base confirms b6a5eceb is the reviewed head on the node branch, not an ancestor of this worktree's HEAD.
